chapters.reason: The paper analyzes how a standard two-layer transformer, through training on ICL tasks, develops an induction head mechanism without architectural modifications, fitting the description of training-induced recurrence.

The study provides a micro-level analysis showing distinct computational roles for each layer (copier, selector, classifier) in the reasoning process, aligning with clear correspondence between layer depth and reasoning.

The intermediate layers (specifically the feed-forward network) are shown to act as a selector that distills essential information from relevant tokens, forming a core part of the latent reasoning circuit.
